groups.heading: OPTIONAL SOURCE DEPTH
items: European companies were chartered bodies seeking monopoly profits in Asian trade, especially spices, textiles and later revenue-rich territories.
The Portuguese pioneered naval coercion through forts, fleets, the cartaz system and the Estado da India .
The Dutch VOC was commercially formidable but prioritised the Indonesian archipelago
the Amboyna Massacre (1623) worsened English-Dutch rivalry and pushed English attention elsewhere.

groups.heading: ADVANCED DEBATE
items: The English Company gradually built a network of coastal bases: Surat , Madras , Bombay and Calcutta .
The French Company under Colbert developed Pondicherry and Chandernagore , but French state dependence and weaker naval-financial support limited it.
Dupleix showed that European companies could intervene in Indian succession disputes and convert military support into political influence.
The English learned the same techniques but combined them with stronger naval
